claim: For \(L_\alpha=-\Delta+|x|^{2\alpha}\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), \(n\ge3\) and \(\alpha>0\), the critical radius satisfies \(\rho_\alpha(x)\asymp(1+|x|)^{-\alpha}\) and \(i(\rho_\alpha)=\alpha\). For \(0<\theta<1/(1+\alpha)\), \(\gamma>0\), and \(\beta\in\mathbb R\), the symbol \(b_{\gamma,\beta}(x)=(1+|x|)^\gamma[\log(e+|x|)]^\beta\) belongs to \(\mathrm{BMO}^{\log}_{\rho_\alpha,\theta}(\mathbb R^n)\) if and only if \(\gamma<\theta\), or \(\gamma=\theta\) and \(\beta\le0\). In this membership region, the published endpoint theorem yields bounded commutators \([b_{\gamma,\beta},R_j^{L_\alpha}]\) on \(H_{L_\alpha}^1(\mathbb R^n)\), where \(R_j^{L_\alpha}=\partial_jL_\alpha^{-1/2}\); no boundedness claim is made outside the membership region.

correctness.rationale: For \(V_\alpha(x)=|x|^{2\alpha}\), the ball average is comparable to \((|x|+r)^{2\alpha}\), giving \(\rho_\alpha(x)\asymp(1+|x|)^{-\alpha}\). The admissibility exponent is exactly \(\alpha\). For centered balls the mean oscillation is comparable to \(R^\gamma(\log R)^\beta\), forcing \(\gamma<\theta\) or \(\gamma=\theta\) with \(\beta\le0\). The small/intermediate/large-radius estimates prove sufficiency. The operator consequence matches Theorem 4.2's parameter condition after substituting \(\tau(V_\alpha)=\infty\) and \(i(\rho_\alpha)=\alpha\).
